title: Enough K-injectives compute total right derived functors
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $K(\mathcal A)$ be the homotopy category of its cochain complexes (morphisms are chain maps modulo chain homotopy), with localization $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, where a complex $J$ is K-injective when every map from an acyclic complex to $J$ is homotopic to zero [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category and $F:K(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ an exact functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Then the total right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$ exists (with a natural transformation $\eta:F\to RF\circ Q$ such that composition with $\eta$ gives a bijection between natural transformations $RF\to G$ and $F\to G\circ Q$ for every functor $G:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal T$), and every K-injective complex $J$ computes it: the derived-functor comparison $F(J)\to RF(QJ)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 070K, Lemma lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies (literature/stacks-project/derived.tex); computation also Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined

proof.text: For each complex K choose a quasi-isomorphism f_K : K → J_K to a K-injective complex, using the given hypothesis. For each object X of D(A), choose a representative K_X with an isomorphism Q(K_X) ≅ X, using essential surjectivity of the localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put j(X)=J_(K_X). Compose the inverse representative isomorphism with Q(f_(K_X)) and the quotient/localization comparison to obtain e_X : X ≅ Qh(π(j(X))), where π is the homotopy-category quotient. This works for any chosen localization model, without objectwise equality.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y; Hom bijection from Tag 070I. Explicit construction and universal-property verification by E1.

proof.text: The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] defines a unique lift of any map Qh(K) → Qh(π(j(X))) to K → π(j(X)). Define R : D(A) → K(A) by R(X)=π(j(X)) and R(a)=lift(e_X⁻¹ ≫ a ≫ e_Y). Applying Qh and its injectivity on these Hom sets proves preservation of identities and composition: the middle e_Y and e_Y⁻¹ cancel. Set RF=R ⋙ F.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y; Hom bijection from Tag 070I. Explicit construction and universal-property verification by E1.

proof.text: Define u_K : K → R(Qh(K)) as the unique lift of e_(Qh(K)). For a : K → L, apply Qh to a ≫ u_L and u_K ≫ R(Qh(a)); the definition of R and cancellation of e_(Qh(K)) give equal images. Injectivity of the Hom bijection into j(Qh(L)) proves naturality of u. Set η=whiskerRight u F.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y; Hom bijection from Tag 070I. Explicit construction and universal-property verification by E1.

proof.text: When K is K-injective, lift e_(Qh(π(K)))⁻¹ to g : R(Qh(π(K))) → π(K) using the same Hom bijection, this time with K-injective target K. Applying Qh to u_(π(K)) ≫ g and g ≫ u_(π(K)) gives the identity maps by the two inverse identities of e. Injectivity into K and into j(Qh(π(K))) gives the two inverse identities in K(A). Thus u_(π(K)) is invertible, and η_(π(K))=F(u_(π(K))) is invertible.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y; Hom bijection from Tag 070I. Explicit construction and universal-property verification by E1.

proof.text: For any G : D(A) → T and α : F → Qh ⋙ G, define β_X = α_(R(X)) ≫ G(e_X⁻¹). Naturality of α at R(a), the defining formula Qh(R(a))=e_X⁻¹ ≫ a ≫ e_Y, and the inverse identities of e prove naturality of β. Naturality of α at u_K gives F(u_K) ≫ α_(R(Qh(K))) = α_K ≫ G(e_(Qh(K))); composing with G(e_(Qh(K))⁻¹) proves η ≫ whiskerLeft Qh β = α. Hence the map on natural transformations is surjective.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y; Hom bijection from Tag 070I. Explicit construction and universal-property verification by E1.

proof.text: For injectivity, suppose β and γ have equal composites with η. Evaluate this equality at R(X), which is represented by the K-injective j(X). The preceding invertibility of u_(R(X)) implies that η_(R(X)) is an isomorphism, so cancellation gives β_(Qh(R(X))) = γ_(Qh(R(X))). Naturality of β and γ at the isomorphism e_X : X → Qh(R(X)), followed by cancellation of G(e_X), gives β_X=γ_X. Thus composition with η is bijective. Together with the K-injective computation established above, this proves the unchanged conclusion.
